messages:
melissa: Quick follow-up from the postmortem — we keep hitting the same pattern: small config change -> subtle metric drift -> alerts late -> bigger blast radius. Proposing a lightweight canary feedback loop (adaptive sampling + short auto-rollback) to close the gap.

jordan: +1. Can we quantify the drift window? In the last incident metrics started diverging at ~12m but our alerting/debugging chain meant rollback didn't happen until ~40m.

alex: I can own the auto-rollback controller work. Need a clear spec for thresholds and a minimal config format. ETA EOW if we keep scope minimal.

priya: Suggestion: three-tier detection + cap blast radius. Soft alert at 5m with 2x baseline error-rate, hard alert at 10m with 3x -> trigger auto-rollback. Limit canary to 2% traffic by default and gating for increases.

melissa: Good. Also want a rapid-sample escalation: if we see CPU/latency spike + small error bump, double sampling rate for 5m to confirm.

alex: Prototype config below (controller can ingest as JSON). Will open an RFC PR later today.

alex: ```
{
  "canary": {
    "initial_traffic_pct": 1,
    "blast_radius_limit_pct": 2,
    "adaptive_sampling": {
      "metric": "error_rate",
      "soft_threshold_multiplier": 2.0,
      "hard_threshold_multiplier": 3.0,
      "soft_window_seconds": 300,
      "hard_window_seconds": 600
    },
    "auto_rollback": {
      "enabled": true,
      "min_canary_duration_seconds": 120,
      "trigger_on_hard_threshold": true
    }
  }
}
```

priya: This looks actionable. I'll add dashboards and a small synthetic eval to ensure we don't get false positives on noisy endpoints.

melissa: Action items (owners + timelines):
1) alex — implement controller auto-rollback & rapid-sample mode, create RFC + PR, due 2026-03-30.
2) priya — telemetry dashboards, synthetic evals, and gating rules, due 2026-04-02.
3) sam — update runbook, add drill plan and schedule a tabletop, due 2026-04-06.
4) melissa — coordinate release-safety sync and run the first canary drill, target 2026-04-10.

sam: I'll add the runbook changes and schedule the drill. Will include a checklist: pre-rollout canary metrics, rapid-sample toggles, rollback contacts.

oncall-bot: Incident bot: scheduled canary-safeguard test for 2026-04-10 15:00 UTC. Reminder 48h prior.

jordan: Also propose we add a weekly aggregation to surface "near misses" (2x short spikes that didn't trigger rollback) so we can tune thresholds rather than chasing one-off noise.

melissa: Agreed — add "near-miss" dashboard panel to the telemetry ticket.

alex: I'll create tickets and link infra tests to the PR: INF-4321 (auto-rollback impl), INF-4322 (telemetry + dashboards), OPS-987 (runbook & drill). Will post links in the RFC.

priya: Ping me when the RFC is up, I'll review and iterate on dashboard panels. Also will run perf tests against edge endpoints to check false-trigger rates.

melissa: Thanks team. We'll review progress in the release-safety sync Friday 09:00. If anyone hits blockers ping #eng-oncall or @melissa. :thumbsup:

alex: PR opened: https://git.redwood.ai/r/inf/auto-rollback-rfc (WIP) — will assign reviewers.

priya: Reviewing now, leaving comments on sampling rates.

melissa: Nice work. Let's keep this lightweight and measurable; primary goal is to shrink detection->rollback to <15m for critical regressions.
